title: Admin Command Provenance Layer & Replay Sandbox
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Operators run ad-hoc admin commands and scripted playbooks against live clusters; when incidents recur we lack deterministic provenance that ties a human or automated action to an observed state. Reproducing operator workflows currently requires reading logs, guessing flags, and relying on memory. This increases time-to-resolution, blocks post-incident analysis, and raises safety concerns for sensitive actions.

Proposed solution: Implement a lightweight 'provenance layer' that sits in front of admin utilities and records an event-sourced, cryptographically hashed action stream. Each admin action will be recorded as a signed metadata capsule (actor, dry-run flag, command template, redaction hints, env fingerprint, model of input tokens) plus an execution trace pointer. Separately, build a replay sandbox service (read-only by default) that can deterministically re-run actions against a synthetic environment: cached KV snapshots, mock model responses, and reversible network stubs. The sandbox supports safe live replay with RBAC gating, an interactive step-through UI in the Console, and an audit export for postmortems.

Key design choices and trade-offs:
- Event-sourcing vs inline audit logs: event-sourcing enables deterministic replay and compact storage but requires careful schema migration; we accept the migration cost for replayability.
- Cryptographic signing of actions: adds trust and non-repudiation for enterprise customers, but increases key management surface area; will integrate with KMS keys scoped to the org.
- Redaction vs fidelity: recordings will include redact hints and a scrubber pipeline; we will not store raw secrets. Replay fidelity prioritized for control-plane actions; noisy debug I/O is optional.
- Performance: recording must be async and non-blocking for live admin flows; initial implementation uses append-only Kafka topic + index store.

Deliverables: provenance capture library (small Go shim for existing admin CLIs), event store schema, replay sandbox backend, Console UI for interactive replays, PRD and runbook examples, initial integration with our RBAC+KMS stack.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance shim available as a Go module with README and 3 example integrations (admin-cli, opsctl, support-shell)
Actions are captured in event store with schema v1 including actor, template, env-fingerprint, redact-hints, and execution-outcome
Replay sandbox can execute a recorded action in synthetic mode and reproduce side-effect-free sequencing for control-plane flows
Console UI shows action timeline with diffable pre/post snapshots and a 'step-through' button gated by RBAC
Secrets are scrubbed by the scrubber pipeline and verified via unit tests and a fuzz test harness
Security review completed and KMS integration documented for signing keys

implementation_notes: Start with non-blocking capture: shim writes to local WAL and ships to Kafka in a best-effort background worker
Schema v1 will be intentionally conservative: avoid embedding large payloads; store pointers to snapshot store
Replay sandbox uses containerized mock services and a snapshot playback engine (reuse existing chronos-runbook-scheduler patterns)
RBAC gating: replay endpoints default to 'read-only' role; elevated replay with write-emulation requires entitlements and an approval step
Testing: create reproducible harness that runs 100 recorded actions against sandbox and asserts state-idempotence
